findings.title: Mutual-exclusion validation between `age` and `timestamp` fails on `0` or when both are omitted
findings.body: `BrowserReportSerializer` marks both `age` and `timestamp` as `required=False` and uses field-level validators (`validate_timestamp` and `validate_age`) that check `if self.initial_data.get("age"):` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):`. This has two bugs: (1) `0` is a valid value for both `age` (a report delivered immediately has `age: 0`) and `timestamp` (`min_value=0`), but `0` is falsy in Python, so a payload containing both fields where one is `0` bypasses the validator; (2) in DRF, field-level `validate_<field>` methods are not called when a field is omitted, so a report missing both `age` and `timestamp` passes validation. This check should be performed in an object-level `validate(self, attrs)` method checking `"age" in attrs` vs `"timestamp" in attrs`.

findings.title: `fetch_error_details` pairs `error_ids` with `events.values()` positionally instead of by `node_id`
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` calls `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then iterates over `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `get_multi` returns a `dict` keyed by `node_id` whose key order is not guaranteed to match `node_ids` (for example when some keys are served from cache or returned in storage order, or if missing keys are omitted). Iterating with `zip(error_ids, events.values())` can associate an `event_id` with the wrong event's data; each `node_id` should be looked up via `events.get(node_id)`.

findings.title: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` are only filtered out when a search query is entered
findings.body: In `Attributes`, `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` early when `!searchQuery.trim()`, and only applies `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` inside the `sorted.filter(...)` call when `searchQuery` is non-empty. Consequently, `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` remain visible by default and are only hidden after the user types into the search bar.

findings.title: `renderDefaultHeadCell` computes alignment from display `column.name` instead of `column.key` and `tableData.meta.fields`
findings.body: `renderDefaultHeadCell` calls `fieldAlignment(column.name, column.type as ColumnValueType)`. When custom `columns` are passed with a human-readable `name` (e.g. `'Count of Span Duration'`) and the optional `type` field on `TabularColumn` is omitted, `fieldAlignment` cannot recognize the aggregate/field from the display label and defaults the header alignment to `'left'`, whereas `renderDefaultBodyCell` resolves the renderer using `column.key` and `tableData.meta.fields` and right-aligns numeric cells. `fieldAlignment` should be called with `String(column.key)` and fall back to `tableData?.meta.fields`.
